cross_criterion_notes: The design correctly uses 150°C (batch reference) as the first screening temperature rather than the published flow optimum of 170°C; this is a defensible conservative choice but the 170°C optimum should be noted as a priority next step.

The 4 mm ID packed-bed cartridge creates real axial dispersion concerns (low Pe) and potential external mass-transfer limitations (Da>>1 flagged) that are acknowledged but not quantitatively resolved; these are appropriate screening uncertainties.

The nominal residence time basis (geometric volume / liquid flow = 0.6 min) is correctly distinguished from actual packed-bed contact time, which is unknown without RTD measurement; the proposed VAL-RTD experiment appropriately addresses this.
Single-stream premix design is chemically justified since benzyl azide and phenylacetylene are stable without Cu catalyst at room temperature; no separate feed streams are required.
All arithmetic closes exactly per the deterministic verification sheet with zero relative error on the residence time index.
